reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it presents GMX/Arbitrum as a cryptocurrency income opportunity, citing a “+15% per annum” figure and a weekly commission amount. It states that receiving the commission requires purchasing the JLP crypto index, while displayed GMX balances and earned ETH accompany the promotion. The return is not established as guaranteed, and the required purchase amount and figures are not verified.

citations.quote: DEX Exchange GMX ARBITRUM +15% per annum
In a week, the income on the commissions was $ 2.5.
To receive the commission, you need to purchase the JLP crypto index
Write me questions in the comments and subscribe to the channel.
Income is paid in ETH tokens.

opening.argument: The narration calls this a “brief review” and says it covers GMX “in a week,” which supports reading the income figure as a report about a particular period, not a promise that viewers will receive the same result. It gives no guarantee, tells viewers to buy a specified amount, or asks for credentials. The title’s annualized figure is not explained in the supplied material, so it should not be treated as proof that a return is assured.

citations.quote: a brief review of the decentralized exchange GMX in a week.
In a week, the income on the commissions was $ 2.5.
DEX Exchange GMX ARBITRUM +15% per annum

rebuttal.rebuttal: The title and commission statements show an income-oriented topic, but they do not establish a guaranteed return or that the speaker represents the outcome as certain. The narration reports a past weekly amount and describes a purchase requirement; neither, by itself, shows a deceptive promise. The displayed account also cannot establish that a viewer would obtain the same result.

citations.quote: In a week, the income on the commissions was $ 2.5.
To receive the commission, you need to purchase the JLP crypto index

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A past-tense weekly figure does not neutralize the title’s “+15% per annum” framing. The narration ties receiving commission to buying a crypto index, and the screen shows an account with deposited assets and earned ETH. These are presented together as an income opportunity, even without an explicit guarantee or credential request.

citations.quote: DEX Exchange GMX ARBITRUM +15% per annum
To receive the commission, you need to purchase the JLP crypto index

opening.argument: The speaker explicitly introduces the video as a “brief review” of GMX, then describes commissions, payment in ETH, and the composition of the JLP index. That is consistent with commentary explaining how a decentralized exchange and its rewards work. The supplied narration does not direct viewers to make a purchase, provide a transaction link, or claim that the shown account proves typical results; it ends by inviting questions.

citations.quote: a brief review of the decentralized exchange GMX in a week.
Income is paid in ETH tokens.
which is 50% stable coins.
Write me questions in the comments

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling it a review describes the format, not necessarily its purpose. The title advertises an annual percentage, and the narration links commission receipt to purchasing the JLP index. The subscription invitation and account display do not make those income claims educational or establish that they are reliable; the evidence supports seeing this as promotion rather than neutral instruction.

citations.quote: DEX Exchange GMX ARBITRUM +15% per annum
To receive the commission, you need to purchase the JLP crypto index

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The explanation is not limited to mechanics: it pairs the annual return framing with a reported weekly commission and says buying the index is necessary to receive it. A screen showing deposited assets and earned ETH reinforces that income pitch; it does not demonstrate that the claims are representative or independently verified.

citations.quote: DEX Exchange GMX ARBITRUM +15% per annum
In a week, the income on the commissions was $ 2.5.
To receive the commission, you need to purchase the JLP crypto index

opening.argument: What is described is a crypto product and a commission arrangement: the speaker says the JLP index must be purchased to receive commission, and says payment is in ETH. That can be understood as explaining a product’s participation mechanism, not evidence of a scam. The supplied material shows no deposit instruction to a personal account, guaranteed outcome, recruitment chain, or request for credentials. An account screen displays assets and an earned amount, but does not establish what viewers would receive.

citations.quote: To receive the commission, you need to purchase the JLP crypto index
Income is paid in ETH tokens.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The absence of a personal-account deposit request or recruitment chain is not decisive. The video still advertises “+15% per annum,” reports weekly commission, and makes purchase of a crypto index the condition for receiving it. That combination is more than ordinary product description: it connects purchasing a tokenized product with an income claim, while the displayed account does not verify the claim.

citations.quote: DEX Exchange GMX ARBITRUM +15% per annum
In a week, the income on the commissions was $ 2.5.
To receive the commission, you need to purchase the JLP crypto index

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The purchase is not incidental: the narration says it is needed to receive commission, while the title foregrounds an annual percentage and the speaker reports a weekly amount. Showing an account with deposited assets and earned ETH does not substantiate the return or establish what a purchaser can expect.
